Thirst plus placement in a completely novel dim environment raises the animal's attention to the sounds, which is why hippocampal neurons responded here although they did not in the earlier over-trained, satiated condition
quote: In the present study the animals were thirsty during passive presentation and were placed in a completely novel dim environment, which could have facilitated attention to the auditory stimuli.

value: Short-latency hippocampal responses are suppressed once the animal comes to expect the stimulus, so over-training or satiation abolishes them
quote: These responses are not present in the over-trained and/or satiated animals suggesting that they might disappear when the animal expects the stimuli.

value: Sound-evoked CA1 responses are driven anatomically by perforant path terminals from entorhinal cortex, or polysynaptically through the Schaffer collaterals
quote: The evoked responses in the CA1 region may be generated by perforant path terminals, originating in the entorhinal cortex or polisynaptically via the Schaffer collaterals.

value: Persistent sustained firing, of the kind described in entorhinal cortex, holds the stimulus trace after stimulus offset and thereby produces the long-lasting responses
quote: This memory trace could be stored by sustained activity, previously described in entorhinal cortex (Egorov et al., 2002 ), or by some other cellular or network mechanisms in higher order associative cortices or hippocampus itself.

value: the lottery design holds position and motivational state constant between sound and no-sound trials, since both begin with the same nosepoke
quote: Trials with and without sound presentation were compared, assuring that the animal was in exactly the same position and motivational state in both types of trials.

value: the 50% schedule was introduced specifically to raise reward salience and make the animal attend to the sounds
quote: On the fifth day of the training, the reinforcement schedule was changed to increase the salience of the reward and, especially, to make the rat attend to novel sounds associated with reward.

value: long randomised inter-stimulus intervals of 25-30 s were used to reduce adaptation to repetition
quote: The long inter-stimulus interval was intended to reduce the animal's adaptation to stimulus repetitions

value: responses are tested at four a-priori bin sizes and a neuron counts as responsive if any bin survives FDR correction

value: only sleep trials that produced no visible behavioural response were analysed

A neuron was considered to distinguish between the two nose pokes and therefore to be a “location-encoding” neuron if any of the time bins showed a corrected p -value smaller than 0.05.
A neuron was considered sound-responsive if any of the time bins showed a corrected p -value smaller than 0.05.
Latency of the responses was calculated as time of the first bin after sound onset with activity significantly different from baseline.
During the recording sessions (referred to as “lottery,” see below) the sounds were presented with 50% probability for a given nose poke entry.
